did_you_know.text: The vision was given to Daniel in the third year of the reign of Cyrus, king of Persia. It is described as a true message and as a vision requiring understanding.
Before the vision, Daniel mourned for three full weeks.
During those three weeks, Daniel ate no choice food, meat, or wine, and he did not anoint himself with oil.
The vision took place on the twenty-fourth day of the first month, while Daniel was standing beside the great river, the Tigris.
The figure Daniel saw was dressed in linen and wore a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist.
The figure is described with a radiant and powerful appearance: his face was like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, and his limbs like polished bronze.
Only Daniel saw the vision. The people with him did not see it, but they were overcome by great fear and ran away to hide.

The messenger explained to Daniel that his prayer had been heard from the very first day, but he was delayed for twenty-one days by the prince of the kingdom of Persia, until Michael came to help him.
The purpose of the mission was to explain to Daniel what would happen to his people in the latter days, because the vision concerns days yet to come.
The vision presents a struggle between the princes of the kingdoms: the messenger was about to return to fight the prince of Persia, and he announced that the prince of Greece would come.
